findings.title: HTTPS certificate
findings.detail: The certificate expires in 20 days (2026-11-06).
findings.recommendation: Check that automatic renewal is in place.

findings.title: TLS protocol version
findings.detail: Connection negotiated with TLSv1.3.

findings.title: HTTP to HTTPS redirect
findings.detail: The site is still reachable over unencrypted HTTP, without a redirect.
findings.recommendation: Set up a permanent (301) redirect from HTTP to HTTPS.

findings.title: Content-Security-Policy
findings.detail: Missing: no limit on which scripts the page can load (protection against XSS injection).
findings.recommendation: Define a CSP suited to the site, starting in "Report-Only" mode.

findings.title: Cookies
findings.detail: No cookies set on the home page.

findings.title: HSTS
findings.detail: Missing: the browser is not required to use HTTPS on later visits.

findings.title: Referrer-Policy
findings.detail: Missing: browsers apply their default policy (strict-origin-when-cross-origin in recent versions).

findings.title: Subresource Integrity
findings.detail: No scripts on the home page.

findings.title: X-Content-Type-Options
findings.detail: Present (nosniff).

findings.title: Clickjacking protection
findings.detail: The site can be displayed inside a frame on another site (clickjacking risk).
findings.recommendation: Add "X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN" or "frame-ancestors 'self'" in the CSP.

findings.title: Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy
findings.detail: Not set (optional; earns bonus points when set).

findings.title: Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy
findings.detail: Not set (optional; earns bonus points when set).

findings.title: Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy
findings.detail: Not set (optional; earns bonus points when set).

findings.title: Permissions-Policy
findings.detail: Missing: no restriction on access to browser features (camera, microphone, geolocation).
findings.recommendation: Add for example "Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()".

findings.title: Software version disclosure
findings.detail: The server announces its versions (Server: Apache/2.4.41 (Ubuntu); X-Powered-By: PHP/7.4.3), which helps an attacker target known vulnerabilities.
findings.recommendation: Hide version numbers in the server configuration.

findings.title: Mail servers (MX)
findings.detail: 2 server(s): mx1.hosting-example.com, mx2.hosting-example.com

findings.title: SPF (authorized senders)
findings.detail: The SPF record ends with "?all" (neutral): it provides almost no protection.
findings.recommendation: Move to "~all", then "-all" once your senders are listed.

findings.title: DMARC (anti-spoofing policy)
findings.detail: "none" policy: DMARC monitors but blocks nothing.
findings.recommendation: After a few weeks of report analysis, move to "quarantine", then "reject".

findings.title: DMARC: reports
findings.detail: No report address (rua): you cannot see who sends email on your behalf.

findings.title: DKIM (email signing)
findings.detail: No DKIM key found among the common selectors tested (16). This is not necessarily a problem: the selector may have another name.
findings.recommendation: Check in your email service (Google Workspace, Microsoft 365...) that DKIM signing is enabled.

findings.title: MTA-STS (encrypted email delivery)
findings.detail: Not set: other mail servers may deliver your incoming email without encryption if an attacker tampers with the connection.
findings.recommendation: Publish an MTA-STS policy (in "testing" mode first), or enable it in your email service.

findings.title: TLS reporting (TLS-RPT)
findings.detail: Not set: you are not told when other servers fail to deliver your mail securely.
findings.recommendation: Publish a _smtp._tls TXT record, e.g. "v=TLSRPTv1; rua=mailto:tls-reports@your-domain".

findings.title: DNSSEC
findings.detail: Not enabled for bakery-example.com: DNS answers are not signed, so a resolver cannot detect forged answers (redirecting visitors or emails to another server).
findings.recommendation: Enable DNSSEC at your DNS host, then publish the DS record at your registrar (often a single option in their interface).

findings.title: CAA (allowed certificate authorities)
findings.detail: No CAA record: any certificate authority may issue a certificate for this domain.
findings.recommendation: Publish a CAA record naming the authority you use, e.g. 0 issue "letsencrypt.org".
